finding_dispositions.note: I re-read PL 24 cols. 642-644 and 649 on 300-dpi page images (PDF pp. 325, 326 and 329), rendered from research-0's receipt, which I re-hashed (e55e8bd2, a match). I re-read Aquinas [85023] in the re-hashed Corpus Thomisticum HTML (5300798b) and Nova Vulgata Isaiah 63:17 and Ps 79:4 and 15 in their re-hashed receipts (9c9c78c4, e508ed1c). The verified.md row now has a 'The texts' half and a 'The witnesses' half. The texts: in the Hebrew-based Latin, 63:17b asks God to turn or return and the refrain asks God to turn us. The witnesses: Jerome reads the verse 'Convertere... sive converte nos' at col. 643 and develops the second reading 'juxta Septuaginta' through col. 644. The col. 649 quotation of Ps 79:4 is now 'also', one of Jerome's ties and not the only one. Aquinas adduces Ps 89:13 and Lam 5:21 together under one petition for mercy, and 'separately' is gone. The same account is in scope 3.3 (Jerome row, Aquinas row now citing [85023], and the rewritten paragraph 'two petitions to turn, joined by the witnesses'), in Reading 3's psalm row (class column naming each witness and its text: Jerome's Latin of the Hebrew and of the Septuagint; Aquinas on the Vulgate), in Reading 3's Jerome and Aquinas bullets and limits, and in the interpretations header, which no longer says 'keep apart'. One correction to the review's gloss, decided by the page image: Jerome's lemma at col. 642 gives the verse both from the Hebrew and from the Septuagint, and both of his Latin renderings read 'convertere propter servos tuos'. There is no 'converte propter servos tuos' at col. 644. So the record says 'turn us' is Jerome's reading of the petition, developed with the Septuagint's added clause 'ut modicum possideamus montis sancti tui'. It does not say the Septuagint has a different verb. The Greek was not read, and the record says so. Reading 1 does not use the join: its moral sense cites the refrain alone. A sweep of scope, interpretations, context, verified.md and the instance manifest finds no sentence saying or implying that the Fathers keep the petitions apart.

summary: I repaired RES-TXT-003. The psalm-to-first-reading row in propers/verified.md, scope section 3.3 (the Jerome and Aquinas rows and the 'two petitions' paragraph) and Reading 3 in interpretations.md now keep the textual observation and add what the witnesses do with it. Jerome reads Isaiah 63:17 as 'Convertere, ait, Domine, sive converte nos', developing the second reading with the Septuagint's clause (PL 24 cols. 643-644), and also quotes Ps 79:4 at 64:7 (col. 649). Aquinas sets Lam 5:21 'converte nos' beside Ps 89 'convertere' under Isaiah's 'convertere' ([85023]). I also cleared all four advisories and regenerated the chronology record and annotations; only the verified.md fingerprint changed.
